title: U.S. Senate · Idaho

context.text: David Roth won the May 19, 2026 Democratic primary for this seat (61.9% of the vote) but is listed by Ballotpedia as withdrawn or disqualified and does not appear as a candidate in the November 3 general election.
Jim Risch defeated Josh Roy, Joe Evans, and Denny LaVe in the May 19, 2026 Republican primary with 67.3% of the vote.

summary.text: Jim Risch is the incumbent Republican U.S. Senator from Idaho, first elected in 2008 and now serving his third term. A lawyer and rancher by background, he spent decades in Idaho politics as a county prosecutor, state senator, lieutenant governor and, briefly, governor before joining the Senate. According to his Senate website, he chairs the Foreign Relations Committee and also serves on the Energy and Natural Resources, Small Business and Entrepreneurship, Intelligence and Ethics committees.

background.text: Born in Milwaukee, Wisconsin. He attended the University of Wisconsin-Milwaukee from 1961 to 1963 before moving to the University of Idaho.
Received a bachelor's degree in forestry (1965) and a law degree (1968) from the University of Idaho, where he served on the Law Review.

Won election as Ada County Prosecuting Attorney in 1970, serving two terms. During that time he taught criminal justice classes at Boise State and served as president of the state prosecuting attorneys' association.

Was first elected to the Idaho Senate in 1974 and served there for many years, where his Republican colleagues chose him as Majority Leader and President Pro Tempore. He lost a 1988 re-election bid and returned to the chamber in 1995 by appointment.
Was twice elected Idaho's Lieutenant Governor, first in 2002 and again in 2006.

Became Idaho's 31st Governor on May 26, 2006, when Gov. Dirk Kempthorne resigned to become U.S. Secretary of the Interior, and served the remaining months of the term. According to his Senate website, his governorship included property tax reform that cut property taxes by 20% and $100 million in additional funding for public schools.
Was elected to the U.S. Senate in 2008, defeating former U.S. Rep. Larry LaRocco, and took office in January 2009. He was re-elected in 2014 and 2020.
In the Senate, he serves as Chairman of the Foreign Relations Committee and sits on the Energy and Natural Resources, Small Business and Entrepreneurship, Intelligence, and Ethics committees.

Outside public service, he is a rancher, small business owner, and former senior partner in the Risch Goss Insinger Gustavel law firm. According to his Senate website, he and his wife, Vicki, live on a ranch outside Boise and have three sons and nine grandchildren.

priorities.text: Lists protecting the Second Amendment, advocating for energy independence, blocking federal overreach, and defending Idaho agriculture and natural resources among his priorities in the Senate.

positions.summary: His official Senate website lists 'protecting the Second Amendment' among the priorities that define his record in the Senate.

record.text: Chairman of the Senate Foreign Relations Committee.
Serves on the Senate Committee on Energy and Natural Resources, the Committee on Small Business and Entrepreneurship, the Select Committee on Ethics, and the Select Committee on Intelligence.
As Governor of Idaho (2006-2007), cut property taxes by 20% and secured $100 million in additional funding for Idaho's public schools, according to his official Senate biography.

candidates.name: Matt Loesby

summary.text: Matt Loesby is the Libertarian Party nominee for U.S. Senate in Idaho. A software engineer and video game developer, he ran as the Libertarian candidate for Idaho's 1st Congressional District in 2024.

background.text: Born in Glenwood Springs, Colorado.
Earned a bachelor's degree from Chapman University in 2010.
Works as a software engineer. In a 2024 Ballotpedia survey he described himself as a video game developer and software engineer.
Was the Libertarian candidate for Idaho's 1st Congressional District in 2024, receiving 9,594 votes (2.1%) in a race won by Rep. Russ Fulcher.
Advanced unopposed from the May 19, 2026 Libertarian primary for U.S. Senate with 855 votes.

candidates.researchNotes: No campaign website, Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey, or public policy statements found beyond a brief Ballotpedia biography.

candidates.name: Todd Achilles

summary.text: Todd Achilles is an Independent candidate for U.S. Senate in Idaho. An Army veteran and technology executive who also teaches public policy, he was appointed to the Idaho House in 2024 and resigned in 2025 to run for the Senate. In his Ballotpedia survey, he lists his campaign priorities as stopping corruption in Congress, strengthening the middle class and protecting public lands.

background.text: Says he grew up on a family farm.

Earned a B.A. in economics and international relations from Claremont McKenna College, an M.B.A. and a master's in international studies from the University of Washington, and an M.P.A. from the University of California, Berkeley.
Served in the U.S. Army from 1992 to 1995; describes himself as a U.S. Army tank commander and armor officer.

Spent more than 20 years in senior roles at technology companies, according to his own account at T-Mobile, Hewlett-Packard and several startups; Ballotpedia lists his experience as including executive director of product management at T-Mobile, president at HTC, vice president/general manager at HP and CEO of Evoca.
Founded Veterans for Idaho Voters and has worked as a professor.

Was appointed to the Idaho House of Representatives (District 16B) in February 2024 to replace Rep. Colin Nash (D), and was elected to the seat in November 2024, defeating Jackie Davidson with 59.8% of the vote. He served on the Agricultural Affairs, Commerce and Human Resources, Ways and Means and State Affairs committees.
Resigned from the Idaho House in 2025 to launch his U.S. Senate campaign; he lives in Boise with his family, according to his Ballotpedia survey.

priorities.text: Says stopping corruption in Congress is his first priority, citing support for term limits, getting money out of elections, overturning Citizens United, banning congressional stock trading, ending the revolving door between Congress and lobbying, and stopping gerrymandering.
priorities.quote: Washington is broken because politicians answer to parties and donors instead of voters.

priorities.text: Says he would work to strengthen the middle class through measures including shrinking the national debt, breaking up monopolies, eliminating corporate and high-income tax loopholes, and raising wages by rolling back right-to-work laws.
Prioritizes protecting Idaho's public lands, including preserving access, investing in conservation and land management, and supporting rural economies tied to outdoor recreation.

positions.summary: Supports eliminating corporate and high-income tax loopholes as part of a plan to strengthen the middle class.
positions.quote: eliminating corporate and high income tax loopholes

record.text: Voted no on H668 (banning public funds, including Medicaid and state employee insurance, from paying for gender-transition treatment), which passed the Idaho House 58-11 on March 11, 2024.
Voted no on H599 (prohibiting ballot harvesting and setting penalties for violations), which passed the Idaho House 58-11 on March 11, 2024.

candidates.researchNotes: Positions drawn from his Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey; no independent campaign website content reviewed. Achilles was appointed to the Idaho House on February 17, 2024 (replacing Colin Nash) and served roughly one term before resigning in July 2025 to run for U.S. Senate, limiting his record of recorded floor votes.

candidates.name: Natalie Fleming

summary.text: Natalie Fleming is an Independent candidate for U.S. Senate from Idaho. She describes herself as a rancher's daughter and mother with a background in software and information technology, and an author of two books. Her campaign focuses on limits on surveillance and AI, housing affordability and restoring the water cycle.

background.text: Born in Portland, Oregon, and describes herself as a rancher's daughter from Idaho's high desert.
Graduated from Moscow High School and returned to Idaho in 2002 as a single mother, working in software while caring for family members with special needs, by her own account.

Earned a bachelor's degree from Boise State University in 2024, with degrees she describes as in Information Technology Management, Supply Chain Management and Cybersecurity, after returning to school during COVID.
Her career experience includes work as an information technology professional.
Has written two books, one on defying hate propaganda and one on restoring the water cycle.

priorities.text: Says she is running to rein in authoritarianism and mass surveillance, including opposing tracking technology and calling for limits on AI and data brokers.
priorities.quote: I'll push for real limits on AI, an end to mass surveillance in every form, and a tech industry that answers to the people it serves instead of building the infrastructure to control them.

priorities.text: Prioritizes what she calls household security: reducing housing costs driven by institutional investors buying single-family homes, and using degraded federal land for housing instead.
Supports restoring Idaho farmland and rangeland through regenerative grazing and land policy that rewards restoration over extraction.

candidates.researchNotes: Positions drawn from her Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey; no independent campaign website content reviewed. None of her stated priorities map cleanly onto the guide's fixed issue list, so no Position entries were added.
